provenance.note: Curated flagship register; the HMDA register supplies each body's gazetted notification status.

note: Hand-compiled flagship register for Hyderabad, feeding compute-restoration-priority-hyderabad.ts. Areas and coordinates are COMPUTED from the in-repo OSM layer (public/geojson/hyderabad-water-bodies-current.geojson) unless noted. Legal status is read from the in-repo HMDA gazetted register (public/data/hyderabad-lake-register.json). IMPORTANT LIMITATION: the HMDA register covers the 'Extended HMDA Area' survey and does NOT include several of the city's largest and best-known lakes - only 8 of the 20 largest named OSM bodies appear in it, and Hussain Sagar, Himayat Sagar, Shamirpet and Ameenpur are absent entirely. 'not_in_hmda_register' below means exactly that and must not be read as 'unprotected' - those lakes sit under other authorities. Historical claims carry their source; where a commonly-repeated claim could not be substantiated it is omitted rather than hedged.

bodies.name: Osman Sagar
bodies.era: Asaf Jahi (Nizam VII); construction begun 1913, completed 1918
bodies.builder: Hyderabad State, on M. Visvesvaraya's recommendation as Special Consulting Engineer (appointed 15 April 1909)
bodies.feed: Impounds the Musi upstream of the city
bodies.status: Live drinking-water source. Supplied 108.831 MLD on 25 July 2026 - about 4% of the city's draw - and has been drawn on every day since 2020.
bodies.cultural_note: Built as FLOOD CONTROL first and water supply second, after the Great Musi Flood of 28 September 1908 damaged some 59,000 houses. Visvesvaraya's brief was to hold back 'all floods in excess of what the river channel could carry'. Its catchment was protected by GO 111 from 1996 until the order was repealed in 2022.
bodies.location_basis: OSM polygon centroid; 1,810.0 ha computed from the in-repo OSM layer

bodies.name: Himayat Sagar
bodies.era: Asaf Jahi; the second of the twin reservoirs, following Osman Sagar
bodies.builder: Hyderabad State, same post-1908 flood-control programme
bodies.feed: Impounds the Esi (Isa), a Musi tributary
bodies.status: Live drinking-water source; supplied 61.371 MLD on 25 July 2026.
bodies.cultural_note: The Esi is barely mapped - OpenStreetMap carries a single 10 km way for the river Himayat Sagar impounds, against 244 km for the Musi. That is a gap in the public record, not a statement about the river.
bodies.location_basis: OSM polygon centroid; 1,492.5 ha computed from the in-repo OSM layer

bodies.name: Hussain Sagar
bodies.builder: Built during the reign of Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah
bodies.feed: Dug on a tributary of the Musi
bodies.status: The city's signature urban lake and the third largest water body in the metro at about 456 ha.
bodies.cultural_note: Predates the founding of Hyderabad itself by more than two decades - the water came first, the city afterwards. Not present in HMDA's gazetted lake register.
bodies.location_basis: OSM polygon centroid; 456.0 ha computed from the in-repo OSM layer

bodies.name: Mir Alam Tank
bodies.builder: Commissioned by Diwan Mir Alam; planned in the circle of Michel Joachim Marie Raymond, executed by a French engineering company
bodies.status: Survives at about 142 ha inside the Nehru Zoological Park precinct. IN the HMDA register (lake ID 4400, Bahadurpura mandal) with a preliminary notification and NO final notification.
bodies.cultural_note: Twenty-one semicircular masonry arches running roughly 1.5 km - one of the most ambitious pieces of pre-modern waterworks in the Deccan. The frequently repeated claim that it is the world's first multiple-arch dam is NOT asserted here; the sources consulted do not establish it.
bodies.location_basis: OSM polygon centroid; 142.2 ha computed from the in-repo OSM layer

bodies.name: Ameenpur Lake
bodies.era: Qutb Shahi; reportedly built more than 300 years ago during the reign of Ibrahim Qutb Shah (1550-1580)
bodies.builder: Reportedly Abdul Qadir Amin Khan of Patancheru, to water his gardens
bodies.feed: Local catchment, Sangareddy district on the western fringe
bodies.status: Shrunk from more than 300 acres to about 93 acres through encroachment. NOTE a source discrepancy carried deliberately: the in-repo OSM polygon measures 127.3 ha (about 315 acres), which appears to trace the historical extent rather than current water. Both figures are recorded; neither is silently preferred.
bodies.cultural_note: The FIRST water body in India to be declared a Biodiversity Heritage Site, in November 2016 under the Biological Diversity Act 2002. A 2015-16 study documented 166 avian species, 46 herpetofauna, 9 fish and 143 invertebrates.
bodies.location_basis: OSM polygon centroid; see the area discrepancy in status

bodies.name: Durgam Cheruvu
bodies.era: Qutb Shahi period (commonly dated to the era of Golconda's fortifications)
bodies.builder: Not established from the sources consulted
bodies.feed: Rock catchment between Jubilee Hills and Madhapur
bodies.status: About 37 ha, ringed by the IT corridor. IN the HMDA register (lake ID 3706, Serilingampally mandal, Rangareddy) with a preliminary notification and NO final notification.
bodies.cultural_note: Known as the Secret Lake for its concealment among granite outcrops. It now sits at the centre of the highest tanker-demand geography in the city - Madhapur and Kondapur together booked 260,887 tanker loads between January 2022 and February 2024.
bodies.location_basis: OSM polygon centroid; 37.2 ha computed from the in-repo OSM layer

bodies.name: Fox Sagar
bodies.status: About 126 ha. IN the HMDA register (lake ID 2839, Quthbullapur mandal, Medchal-Malkajgiri) with a preliminary notification and NO final notification.
bodies.cultural_note: Also called Jeedimetla Lake. Sits within the northern industrial belt.
bodies.location_basis: OSM polygon centroid; 126.3 ha computed from the in-repo OSM layer

bodies.name: Shamirpet Lake
bodies.status: About 195 ha - the fourth largest water body in the metro. Not present in the HMDA register.
bodies.cultural_note: A Nizam-era retreat lake, now bordered by a deer park.
bodies.location_basis: OSM polygon centroid; 195.2 ha computed from the in-repo OSM layer

bodies.name: Saroor Nagar Lake
bodies.status: About 37 ha in a dense residential quarter of the former LB Nagar zone.
bodies.cultural_note: One of the most-cited examples of sewage inflow into an urban Hyderabad lake.
bodies.location_basis: OSM polygon centroid; 37.1 ha computed from the in-repo OSM layer

bodies.name: Ramanthapur Pedda Cheruvu
bodies.status: IN the HMDA register (lake ID 3811, Uppal mandal, Medchal-Malkajgiri) with a preliminary notification and NO final notification. HYDRAA began restoration works here.
bodies.cultural_note: One of the named lakes in HYDRAA's restoration programme, which is running at a stated ten lakes a year against a 200-lake vision - and a register of 2,978.
bodies.location_basis: No OSM polygon matched; coordinates deliberately null rather than guessed

bodies.name: Nacharam Pedda Cheruvu
bodies.status: The HMDA register carries 'Nacharam Kunta (Erra Kunta)' (lake ID 3806, Uppal mandal) with a preliminary notification and NO final notification. HYDRAA launched a revival here.
bodies.location_basis: No confident OSM polygon match; coordinates null rather than guessed

bodies.name: Edulabad Lake
bodies.feed: Eastern catchment on the Musi system, downstream of the city
bodies.status: About 188 ha - the fifth largest water body in the metro, and downstream of Hyderabad's sewage load.
bodies.cultural_note: Downstream position makes it a natural monitoring point for what the city discharges into the Musi.
bodies.location_basis: OSM polygon centroid; 188.4 ha computed from the in-repo OSM layer

bodies.name: Ibrahimpatnam Cheruvu
bodies.status: About 164 ha in the southern ring.
bodies.cultural_note: Sits in Rangareddy, the district holding 891 register lakes with the weakest legal coverage in the region at 34.5% finally notified.
bodies.location_basis: OSM polygon centroid; 163.9 ha computed from the in-repo OSM layer

bodies.name: Umda Sagar
bodies.feed: South-western catchment, near the twin reservoirs
bodies.status: About 94 ha, inside the belt that GO 111 protected until 2022.
bodies.cultural_note: Its catchment position makes it a direct indicator of what the GO 111 repeal changes on the ground.
bodies.location_basis: OSM polygon centroid; 93.6 ha computed from the in-repo OSM layer
